So for Space Engineers, I'd say it's a great creative "engineering" game (though there's very little actual engineering involved), but I do need to caution anyone reading this, there's no learning curve; it's more of a learning "sheer cliff". Youtubers like Splitsie have helped me get over that learning cliff a little easier. This game will not hold your hand, there is no real story mode, but there are tutorial minigames such as "Learning how to survive". You build, you survive, you make your own goals and achieve them, which makes me think of other construction games like Minecraft, you have to figure things out on your own. I like to consider myself moderately intelligent in the field of engineering, currently I have logged over 300 hours into Space Engineers and I am still learning completely new things that I probably should have known from day 1. That said, you really, really cannot go into this game blind, you will regret doing so. If you're curious about buying this game, I'd say absolutely buy it, the options of what you can do are practically limitless, BUT, look up a beginners guide before playing, it will save you a ton of frustration. Trust me.

To be fair it isn't really an engineering game so much as a creative mechanics game, because while yes, there are logic blocks and mechanical blocks you can use and program, there's hardly any real engineering going on here like you'd find in games such as Besiege. Think more like... if Minecraft was about traversing hostile space and had a wide variety of shapes rather than just blocks. I typically play peaceful games, so my main file is a customized peaceful mode which is nice. The combat of default settings can be rather unforgiving especially if you're new and don't really know what's going to happen. I still need to learn how to print things and how to automate drones, because that is a very complex thing to set up, but beyond that, it's much more of a build-and-destroy type of game, which is why learning how to print things is pretty essential; if your creations get destroyed, you'll save countless hours fixing or remaking them from scratch by learning how to print.
It's fine. Im not addicted to it or anything, I can stop whenever I want.

10/10 — I came for the spaceships, stayed because I apparently enjoy engineering problems

Space Engineers is genuinely one of the best sandbox games I’ve played.

I originally got into it because I wanted to build cool spaceships. And you absolutely can. You can spend hours designing a ship, proudly launch it into space, and then discover that you forgot one tiny thing that makes the entire ship completely useless.

And somehow, that makes it even more fun.

I mostly play multiplayer, and honestly, that’s where a lot of the fun comes from. You meet some really cool people, build ridiculous stuff together, go on adventures, and occasionally watch several hours of work disappear because someone pressed the wrong button.

The community is generally a bit older too. When I first played at 16, I definitely got the occasional “ugh, a kid” reaction, but now that I’m 18, people seem a little more chill. 😂 It’s actually pretty fun finding a group of people to build and mess around with.

The amount of depth in this game is ridiculous. You can build ships, stations, vehicles, factories, weapons, mining operations, or basically whatever insane idea pops into your head. And if the vanilla game somehow isn't enough, there are mods that can make the game even more ridiculous.

There is definitely a learning curve. The game will happily let you spend three hours building something only to discover that your design has the structural integrity of a wet cardboard box.

But when everything finally works?

It feels AMAZING.

Space Engineers is one of those games where you create your own goals and your own stories. Sometimes you're an engineer. Sometimes you're a miner. Sometimes you're a military commander.

And sometimes you're just standing in the middle of your destroyed base wondering where everything went wrong.

I genuinely love this game.

I've really tried extremely hard to enjoy this game. I've tried DLC (which most should've probably been in the main game). I've tried to countless mods, but still not even they could truly ever fill the problems of this game. The only thing I really enjoyed in this game was building ships, but even the most basic parts you need to make your ship look better is behind a DLC. Seriously, I really need to pay extra just so that I can have basic chairs, tables, lockers, and other basic decorations? Shouldn't that be in the main game and can't I just download a mod to do that?

The survival part of this game feels genuinely empty. Sure, there's random encounters, but even they don't make the game feel much alive. Mods basically do all the heavy lifting for this game, just like they do in Farming Simulator. Mods, however, can be cumbersome to deal with, especially in this game. Now, true, maybe they do make it less empty in some DLCS, but some of those DLC's should've came with the game (especially if the DLC all added together is more expensive than the actual game itself). Some DLC is good, but too much DLC, especially some that obviously probably should've reasonably been included in the full game, is unhealthy and definitely a warning sign for players. Like, mods can give you what the DLC can give you.

What also really tells me about what kind of company Keen Software is: Space Engineers 2. Despite it being in early access, Space Engineers 2 is a whopping 30 dollars (for reference, KSP2 in early access costed 50 dollars) and it ALREADY HAS DLC (a 'pioneer' edition, to be exact). Like how do you even already have DLC for a game that's filled with bugs that's in the deepest parts of early access?

Summary:
Space Engineers is a great game, but its treated like a cash cow and the DLC is unreasonable. Its all style with its true meat and potatoes locked behind DLC with the community having to make up for it with its mod, which can easily become cumbersome. Sometimes, whenever I see this game in my Library, I just feel regret about buying it.

Unfortunately, Space Engineers isn't the only game treated like this. Games like Farming Simulator, Stellaris, City Skylines, and other games suffer from the same cash-cow problems (or the Cash Cow Pandemic as I like to call it) and its very likely Space Engineers 2 will face a similar fate. The fact an indie game(s) is mimicking this similar AAA path is somewhat disheartening.

Buy this game if you very much enjoy building huge and useful starships and cool contraptions, but don't expect a good survival experience.

Leaving a positive review because honestly I think the fans complaining about the cosmetic DLCs are a bit over the top. Yes, they've been putting out an increasing number of these, but on the other hand each DLC release coincides with a functional update to the game, adding in new systems and refining others.  Since development on SE2 started, the first game got NPC grids, farming, an economy rework, etc.

Yes, some of that stuff should have been there long before now, BUT considering the sequel is already in early access, seeing them still making significant upgrades to the gameplay of the original is good, and frankly compared to a lot of business practices in gaming I'm OK with throwing them 4 bucks every now and then for new blocks.  (They can absolutely piss off even thinking about adding AI slop, though.)

I'm very strongly reminded of OG Killing Floor - a janky game with a lot of problems but some unique magic, that got content drops every 6 months or so with new maps and features, and some paid DLC characters/weapons alongside those releases to keep ongoing revenue up. I bought every single one, because I loved that game, warts and all. (Or Deep Rock Galactic, for a much more recent and polished example - free content, mostly free cosmetics, occasional optional paid stuff.)

Space Engineers is an extremely flawed game, but it's still doing "Minecraft in space" in a way that I haven't found an alternative to. The "realistic" vibe, the isolation of a deep-space survival map, the feature set. Hell, seeing fully-deformable planets come in was amazing. I might design ugly-ass ships but the feeling of bodging together an idea and seeing it work is great. There's real satisfaction to looking at your gigantic automated warehouse and thinking "I started this with a rover." Being able to write C# scripts directly in game is nuts, the modding support is solid, and the devs have turned common mods into built-in features, like the AI blocks and the evolving NPC support.

The biggest flaw with Spengies is 10000% the UI. It's terrible. Atrocious. Every dedicated Spengies player will install at least one UI mod, probably several. Some aspects of it are decent, and learning key shortcuts helps a lot, but it's still bad, so much so that my best bud won't play the game with me. Step 1, install game. Step 2, install Build Vision.

The block system is simultaneously great and also maddening. Only one block can occupy a space at once, OK that makes sense. But then you try placing a control pedestal on a walkway, or a sign above a railing, and you just...can't. You just can't. On the upside, while you have to run your own conveyors, electricity is magic, so the game doesn't get too frustrating when building.

The main game also doesn't have a point, if you get what I mean? With survival-crafty games, I enjoy them most when I have an objective to work toward, rather than a "do whatever" setup. The game didn't even have any significant hostile mobbery for the longest time, and the backported faction system isn't much to write home about.  The addition of scenarios (mods from the workshop with specific objectives) has helped with that, for sure, so maybe I'm just complaining.

Also, no dedicated server support for Linux? Are you drunk? Who runs dedicated public servers on Windows??

I'm honestly hopeful that they take all the little frustrations from Spengies 1 and fix the majority of them in 2. It's still way too early to tell (despite what the Steam reviews might tell you), but I'll be keeping an eye on it and buying if/when it's ready. If someone makes a better one, I'll go there, but I haven't found it yet.

先说结论：它仍然是你能找到的画面最精致的太空船建造模拟器（除了自家的SE2），但不能当做合格的太空探索游戏来玩。

先说结论的前半部分，作为模拟器，游戏自带了海量的方块可以使用，旋转，伸缩，折叠，各种可动功能都有，星球，太空，无缝衔接，编程块更是实现了要啥功能自己做的可自定义性，如果还不够，还有创意工坊来供玩家选择，建造这一块可以说同类领先，画面曾经过多次改进，现在看也仍然不算落后，美术风格也算得上美观。

然后说后半部分，作为太空探索游戏，十年过去了，它仍然不及格，即使经过了近几年的修修补补，其本质仍然还是当年那个造完船就几乎没事干了的造船模拟器，现在的更新更像是加进去了几个挑战任务来让你测试飞船，还远远谈不上真正的游戏体验。

最后是针对开发组的开发态度，如果说他们没在开发或者不知道玩家想要什么，那是假的，但又很难说得上勤奋，差强人意这个词，可以说是对他们最好的形容，也就是仅仅略微高于及格线，没完全摆烂的程度。

总而言之，就像开头说的，截至目前为止，合格的造船模拟器，失败的太空探索游戏。（顺便祝我自己能活到后半部分也合格的那一天）

相比于其他太空沙盒竞品，这作的优势在于极致的物理设定和自动化编程设定。

通过物流、机械拉力扭矩实现超强物理可塑性。不仅可以造常规的坦克、自行火炮、飞机，打上水mod的情况下航母什么的都不在话下。并且其中大部分的机械动作都可以用基础机械部件手动实现，而不是只能依靠官方提供的高级组件，灵活度很高(当然也很麻烦)。

通过脚本实现的扩展自动化。单是游戏本体就已经提供了不少的自动化方案，而通过脚本能实现无比复杂的视觉、碰撞等逻辑。合成件+自动生产组件+机械部件，我能想象出自动化生产AI机器人工厂的蓝图，更不用说小型无人机自动飞出自动战斗之类的无人战斗体系。

但与之相对的是，创造之后呢？它无法导出，也没有足够智能、强大的敌方AI来提供反馈。甚至缺乏足够的星球内容(比如地下遗迹，比如可交易的聚落)，连探索星球都是如此索然无味。

它适合创造，但只适合创造。

但是就在昨天！我最爱的游戏它涨价了！不是几块钱，也不是十几块钱，不是单独的游戏，也不是一个DLC，而是游戏和所有DLC全部价格翻倍，两周之前还曾经特惠35的本体已经涨价到141，所有DLC也全部涨价到35，相当于曾经买一个本体的钱现在只能买一个DLC。这种打击对一个中年打工人来说无疑是致命的，7个未入库的DLC涨价幅度超过100元。同时SE2的价格也翻倍了，在它还不支持中文的时候，此时的我已经难以形容当时的心情，是失落？是伤心？又或者是什么别的心情。我默默地关上了商店页面，打开SE，开始了一段孤独的旅程。如果K社能看到的话，我希望SE和SE2能够恢复之前的价格，而不是定一个超越一众发达国家的价格（甚至超过了美国区）。我还会继续在SE的旅程，但在目前的定价下，新出的DLC也只能成为我的梦幻泡影了。

SE一直都是一款好游戏，作者从未放弃过更新。从无中文到有中文，从无星球到有星球，从旧版材质到新版材质，制作方真的花了很大心思。
我也曾有很长一段时间沉溺于这游戏里，在地球上找矿挖矿，造飞船，但连大气层都还没出的时候就开学了。而自那次暂停后，我就再也没有心理准备打开它了。
因为它太耗时间，且带来的成就感相对较少。你付出大把时间，可能连一艘小船都造不出。
此外，游戏自由度极高，这点目标的确达到了——但过度自由的世界变得空虚。敌人羸弱，星球上可探索内容少，和Minecraft以及Terraria比起来，SE在这方面彻底败掉了。
因此，我想给制作组提一些目前发展方向的建议：
1.增加星球数量，丰富星球生态环境（如熔岩星球，极寒星球），玩家和建筑、飞船都会真实地受其影响。
2.增加敌对单位数量，增加巢穴种类（如更多敌人的基地，虫巢虫穴等）
3.降低玩家获取资源的困难度（更普遍地生成矿物），扩大玩家携带资源量，简化建筑物所需材料种类。这样既能大幅度提高玩家的游戏效率，也能降低玩家热情消磨的速度。

是我评价最高的游戏，也是我认为最具潜力的游戏，但同时也是一个让人又爱又恨的游戏。
高自由度是SE最大的特征。其自由度之高，个人认为堪比mc。
1.空间自由。全场景可破坏，无缝出入大气层，整个星系任何位置都可去到。
2.玩法自由。可以用物块搭出任何想要的建筑与载具，游戏内置逻辑块与触发块，可实现多种复杂任务（如编程型导弹）。如果认为这还不够，你甚至可以直接在游戏中敲C#代码，实现更复杂的逻辑。

但为何是又爱又恨？因为SE沙盒的纯度太纯了。整个游戏没有明确目标，只有少的可怜的生存要素和探索要素。快节奏的现代生活的人们不会有那么多时间与精力去做缺少目标导向的事情，因此注定了SE是一个不可能大众化的游戏。少有的提升生存与探索体验的mod又因官方的不兼容前版本式的更新而废弃（并非否定官方更新），最终，游戏只能留下那些硬核型玩家，但终究是少数。

啥，你说pve不行还可以pvp？或许SE的高自由度有一个好的底子，但可能因其巨量的cpu运算和pvp玩家数量不足，导致少有服务器能实现pvp，至少国内是这样。

总之，还是期待一下SE2吧。
